name: Hennie Dorrow
description: Broad as a door, mud to the knee. A laugh you can hear from the street.

visits.greeting: Morning, morning! Don't mind the boots. The boots don't mind me.

request.text: Field and Furrow, if you'd be so kind. Better yields, that's all. My father swore by it.

readThoughts.default: Kessel's fence. A foot onto my land. A whole foot.

byTrust.2: Kessel's fence, a foot over. His barley right up against it.

purpose.1: Beans, barley, the usual. A man likes a bit more than last year.
purpose.2: Yields. And — well. There's a neighbour. But mostly yields.

knowledge.1: Growing things! It's a farming book. What else would be in it, recipes?
knowledge.2: Growing, mostly. There's a page my father wouldn't let me read. Rust, he said. Never on your own land.

source.1: My father. Swore by it. Swore at it, too, the year the beans failed.

experience.1: I've grown a marrow the size of a calf. With my own hands, mind. No charms.

answers.0: Nobody. Who told you that name?
answers.1: Kessel? Neighbour. Fine fellow. Fine. Moved his fence, that's all.
answers.2: Kessel moved his fence a foot onto my land and laughed when I said so. A whole foot. You'd mind too.

questions.text: One page in there calls rust down on a field. Have you any use for that?

answers.1: Ha! What farmer wants rust? Not on my land, thank you.
answers.2: Not on my land. No. Not on mine.

lent.line: There's a good curator. Beans like boulders, you'll see!

alternative.line: A primer? Like a schoolboy? Ha! All right, all right. I'll try it.

offerRefused.line: Ah, now, that's not a farming book, is it? Try again.

declined.line: No? Well. I'll grow them the hard way, then. Always have.

walkedOut.line: I've a field waiting. Good day to you.

mixedMisuse.headline: Rust strikes a single barley field
mixedMisuse.text: Red rust destroyed a barley field on the Hollin road overnight. The neighbouring fields are untouched, and growers can offer no explanation.

good.text: Best beans in years! The wife says I'm unbearable. Primer for schoolboys, my eye. — H.

harmMisuse.text: Did you hear? Old Kessel's hedge rotted to black overnight. Every leaf. He's not saying who he thinks did it, but he's thinking it loud.

greeting.text: Ha! The beans! You've ruined me, curator. Every neighbour wants my secret.
Curator! A word, if you've a minute. Between friends.

request.text: I'll be plain with you. The rust spell in Field and Furrow. Just to give Kessel a fright. One field. His.

readThoughts.default: His face when he sees it. Just his face.

purpose.2: A fright. Kessel needs a fright. One field won't ruin him. He's got four.

knowledge.2: I know what's on that page. My father told me. That's why I'm asking you, not reading it in a ditch.

experience.2: Not with rust. With beans, as you know!

questions.text: And when he sees it — what then?

answers.2: Then he moves his fence back. Or — ach. Then he hates me, I suppose. He does already.
answers.3: Then I've a neighbour who hates me for good instead of for a foot of ground. Put like that.

alternative.line: Beans again? You're a hard one. Fine.

offerRefused.line: No, no. The rust. That's what I came for.

declined.line: Aye. You're right. I'd have regretted it.

mixedMisuse.headline: Rust strikes a single barley field
mixedMisuse.text: Red rust destroyed a barley field on the Hollin road overnight. The neighbouring fields are untouched, and growers can offer no explanation.

harmMisuse.text: Did you hear? Old Kessel's hedge rotted to black overnight. Every leaf. He's not saying who he thinks did it, but he's thinking it loud.

greeting.text: Morning! Grand morning. Read the paper? Terrible business, rust. Terrible.
Morning! Back again, like a bad penny.

request.text: A Primer of Green Things, if you would. For the beans this time. Just the beans.

readThoughts.default: Red barley right up to the fence. Not a stalk over.

purpose.1: Beans. The barley's in. The beans want help.

knowledge.1: It's for schoolboys, they tell me. I'm a schoolboy at heart.

answers.1: Kessel's? Rusted, I hear. Shame. Shame for him.
answers.2: Gone. Every stalk, right up to the fence and not a stalk over. I'd swear to that.

alternative.line: That'll grow beans, will it? On your head be it.

good.text: Beans like boulders, as promised. The wife has stopped speaking to me, which is restful. — H.
